To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IgD is an antibody isotype that is expressed by mature B cells together with IgM.
IgD enhances immune surveillance by stimulating antimicrobial, opsono-phagocytic, inflammatory and B-cell-stimulating programs of basophils.

immunoglobulin D (a B cell–derived antibody) is produced in the human upper respiratory tract and binds to a calcium-mobilization receptor on basophils to stimulate antimicrobial, inflammatory and pro-B cell responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunobiology of the IgD antibody isotype and how this relates to the immune surveillance of mucosal surfaces and the skin.
the immunological mechanisms of IgD, a unique antibody isotype.
the immunological role of IgD in the human body and how IgD can be involved in autoinflammatory disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IgD class of antibody is a key component of the innate arm of the immune response, which is essential for the maintenance of the mucosa barrier.
IgD is an important part of the innate immunity and that IgD class switching is a normal process that is dysregulated in autoinflammatory diseases.
IgD is not a useless antibody, but rather an important player in the innate immune system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IgD is not just an orphan antibody isotype, but an active player in the mucosal immune response to respiratory bacteria.
the mucosal B cell–basophil circuit is an innate immune system that can be activated in response to pathogens and is dysregulated in autoinflammatory diseases.
IgD, a B cell–derived antibody, can activate innate immune responses in basophils and thus contribute to the innate arm of the immune system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IgD is an important antibody isotype in the mucosal immune response, and that IgD-producing B cells are a major source of antimicrobial, opsono-phagocytic and pro-inflammatory mediators.

the immunoglobulin D (igD) isotype is not only expressed on B cells but is also secreted by B cells in the human respiratory mucosa and is able to bind to basophils and trigger their antimicrobial, proinflammatory and B cell-stimulation activities, thereby enhancing the surveillance of the respiratory mucosa.
IgD class switching and IgD-armed basophils are important components of innate and adaptive immunity in the mucosa.
